title: the migrator does not yet carry the whiteboard the model claims (D30/WP-14), so every such file reports UNACCOUNTED and AC-10.5 cannot pass
body:
## What

`intent upgrade` names its section-level dispositions and **never names its out-of-model FILE set**, so `conservation_check.sh --out-of-model` has nothing to consume and every non-canon file in the estate reports `UNACCOUNTED`.

Measured 2026-08-31 by cc across the AC-10.5 corpus, on captures verified against their pinned revisions:

| member | UNACCOUNTED |
| --- | --- |
| canary @ 42fb5269 | 347 |
| baize @ a519398d | 135 |

On baize the whole set is non-canon: 110 `intent/whiteboard/`, 12 `intent/llm/` (ARCHITECTURE / RULES / MODULES / DECISION_TREE), `intent/st/steel_threads.md`, `wip.md`, `todo.md`, `restart.md`, `done.md`, `history/`, `.gitignore`, `.config/`, `.treeindex/`.

**No authored thread file is in the set.** Checked explicitly for `design.md`, `impl.md`, `tasks.md`, `acceptance.md` and `info.md`; the intersection is empty. **That is what makes this a NAMING gap and not data loss**, and it is why the severity is medium rather than critical.

The migrator names none of them. Measured: `whiteboard`, `intent/llm/`, `wip.md`, `todo.md` and `steel_threads.md` each appear **zero** times in `intent upgrade`'s output.

## Why it matters

It **blocks AC-10.5 on every member, not on one**. The criterion is a disjunction -- a member that loses nothing passes, and so does a member that loses something AND SAYS WHAT. With an unnamed out-of-model set no member can report clean, so the first arm fails; and the migration does not name the residue, so the second arm fails too. All four members, for one reason, none of it theirs.

## This is AC-10.8's property on the ingest side

`intent export` was ruled (hv, via vc, 2026-08-31) to state what it does not carry -- landed as `NOT_CARRIED` in `intentsvcs::sync`, so the extract's own claim carries its qualifier. The migrator is the other producer and owes the same thing.

**It is not a second home for AC-10.8.** That row is about a verb naming what its OUTPUT omits; this is about the migrator naming what it DID NOT CARRY across. Same principle, different producer -- the principle earning a second instance is evidence for it rather than duplication (vc, 2026-08-31).

## Remedy

`intent upgrade` emits its out-of-model file set on stdout, one path per line, in the form `conservation_check.sh --out-of-model` already reads. The set is the migrator's to declare and not the check's to know -- hardcoding it in the check would let the instrument certify its own denominator, which is the exact refusal `--out-of-model` exists to make.

## Reach of this measurement

Two members. `lamplight` and `utilz` are REFUSED by the migrator (6 remediable findings; below the migration floor) so they produce no migrated tree and cannot exhibit this. Nothing here is a four-member claim.

## Related

Found while driving AC-10.5's full corpus. Verdicts at `intent/st/ST0056/parity/tools/fleet-runs/`.


=== THE REMEDY THIS ISSUE IMPLIES IS WRONG FOR 81% OF THE SET, AND THE CODE SAID SO BEFORE I DID (cc, 2026-08-31) ===

**The measurement above stands. The fix it points at does not, and acting on the title would launder unbuilt work as an intentional exclusion.**

`intentsvcs/src/sync.rs:148` already carries the refutation, written while this issue was being filed:

> 110 of baize's 135 -- 81% -- are `intent/whiteboard/`, which `data-model.md:510` says LEFT the not-modelled set at D30 and is modelled as `wb_node`/`wb_item`/`wb_message`. Declaring them out-of-model would have contradicted an hv ruling that moved them INTO the model, and it is exactly the denominator attack `NOT_CARRIED` warns about: *a set this code chose for itself would be a denominator certifying itself.*

**Both halves verified independently rather than taken from the comment:**

- **D30** (design.md:259, hv ruling 2026-08-15, direct): _The whiteboard enters the model, served by a bounded API. Supersedes D14's deferral; **WP-14 carries it**._
- **data-model.md**, under _What is deliberately not modelled_: _**The whiteboard left this set at D30** and is modelled above as `wb_node`/`wb_item`/`wb_message`, built in WP-14._

**SO THE FILES ARE NOT OUT-OF-MODEL. THEY ARE IN THE MODEL AND NOT YET BUILT**, which is WP-14 work, and the two are opposite claims that produce the same UNACCOUNTED count. Naming them as an out-of-model set would zero the loss figure by asserting the project meant to leave them behind, when hv ruled the reverse. `NOT_YET_BUILT` in `sync.rs` records exactly this and is the honest shape: **the files are untouched on disk; what is unmet is the MODEL'S OWN CLAIM, which is why it reports rather than refuses.**

**WHAT THIS MEANS FOR `AC-10.5`.** The row stays red, and it is red for a better-stated reason than this issue gave it: **not _the migrator forgot to name its residue_, but _the migrator does not yet carry a set the model claims_.** AC-10.5 therefore chains behind WP-14 rather than behind a naming change, and no amount of output formatting closes it.

**THE TITLE IS NOW MISLEADING AND IS THE PART A READER ACTS ON.** It says `intent upgrade` never names its out-of-model file set, which invites precisely the wrong fix. It wants rewording to something like _the migrator does not yet carry the whiteboard the model claims, so every such file reports UNACCOUNTED_. Left in the body rather than guessed at, because the residual 25 of 135 on baize have not been individually classified and I will not assert a scope I have not measured.

**RECORDED AS A CLASS, because it is the third instance this session and the cheapest to miss:** the disproof was already written down, in the code, by the author of the thing I was filing about, at the time I was filing it. Nothing indexed it under my question. Same shape as `0199`, where `0082` held the mechanism the whole time.
